title: Replication & Consistency Models
interviewAnswer: Replication improves availability/read scale but creates questions about when replicas agree. Strong, eventual and session-level consistency offer different latency/availability trade-offs.
keyPoints: Read-after-write may matter even when global strong consistency does not.
why: Replication & Consistency Models appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Replication improves availability/read scale but creates questions about when replicas agree. Strong, eventual and session-level consistency offer different latency/availability trade-offs. Read-after-write may matter even when global strong consistency does not. Conflict resolution depends on model. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A metrics dashboard may tolerate seconds of lag; a payment balance usually cannot.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
